motion.value: 0.26s (panel) / 0.22s (listbox) from opacity 0, translateY(-6px) scale(0.97), origin at anchored corner

motion.name: legend-roll
motion.purpose: Cap legends on layout change, split-flap style.

motion.name: status-tick
motion.purpose: Status counts after an animated update.

motion.name: flash

motion.name: strike
motion.value: 0.24s; key dips 2px and rings in the accent

motion.name: type-out
motion.value: ~20ms per grapheme via requestAnimationFrame, ceil(n/42) graphemes per frame, so ≤ ~0.7s total

motion.name: slip
motion.value: 1.4s; unclip upward, hold 25–75%, lift 6px and fade
motion.purpose: Copied slip rising from the Copy button.

motion.name: chevron
motion.purpose: Picker and settings chevrons when open.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: Output caret while the output has focus.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce → animation/transition durations 0.01ms; @view-transition navigation none; theme wipe skipped; result shown at once

narrative.northStar: The Telegraph Code Book, Typed Out
narrative.overview:
Conversion here is a fixed code table, so the interface is drawn as one: a ruled sheet of paper where every physical key is a cell carrying its source character top-left and its target character bottom-right, and the result is struck into the second pane like a typewriter. The mechanism is visible at all times. The user sees which keys their text used, how often, and what each became, which is why the conversion reads as mechanical rather than guessed. The logo is the same idea at 30px: one keycap with a Latin A top-left and a Thai ก bottom-right.

The material is flat stationery: a tinted ground, a lighter sheet, keycaps one step tonally apart, and 1px ink rules that do all the structural work. There is no texture, no gradient, and no resting shadow. The user picks the stationery: five papers (Parchment, Carbon Copy, Ledger Green, Blueprint, Kraft), each printed in a light and a dark mode. One saturated ink per paper and mode (ink-blue on Parchment light) is held back for the things that are live: struck and used keys, the caret, the primary Copy action, focus, the chosen option. Everything else is the paper's ink and its faded variant.

Density is that of a working tool: one header rule, a heading over a single line of intro, a row of controls, the two-pane frame, a single mono status line, then the full-width code table, two short notes and a one-line credit. Type splits by job: Public Sans speaks the interface, Martian Mono carries anything that is a code, count, label or typed character, and Noto Sans Thai, JP and Hebrew carry the scripts the code table maps into.
keyCharacteristics: Flat ruled stationery; 1px rules in strong ink outline the frames, light rules divide inside them.
One accent per paper and mode, reserved for live state and the single primary action.
Mono for codes, counts, labels and typed text; sans for interface prose.
The code table is the signature: legend top-left, result bottom-right, heat tint from the accent. The keycap logo repeats it.
Motion is mechanical and short: a key strike, a typed-out result, a paper slip, legends rolling like a split-flap board.
Five papers × two modes from one token set; Mode = System follows the OS.

rules.name: The Live Ink Rule
rules.body: The accent marks only what is live or chosen: used and struck keys, the caret, focus, selection, the lead count, the chosen paper and layout, the Auto-detect flash, Copy. The two brand marks (the wordmark slash and the logo's ก) are the only static accent. Nothing else decorative is accent-coloured.

rules.name: The One Token Set Rule
rules.body: Every paper in every mode defines the same eleven role variables and nothing else changes between them; the one optional extra is `--heat-ink`. A new surface reads its colours from the roles, never from a paper's hex values. The only places hex values are written out are the paper swatches in the settings panel (which must preview papers other than the current one) and the static favicon; both must match the stylesheet.

rules.name: The Code Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything the user could read as a code, a count or a typed character is set in Martian Mono with tabular figures where it counts; sentences are set in Public Sans.

rules.name: The Script Fallback Rule
rules.body: Any element that can show user text or a mapped character carries the `--script` stack after its primary face, so Thai, kana and Hebrew render in Noto at matching weight.

rules.name: The Half-Board Rule
rules.body: On a phone the keyboard is never shrunk below legibility; it is cut at the hand split into two stacked half-boards, each row keeping its physical stagger.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces never cast shadows; only the two floating surfaces do (the settings panel and an open listbox), and a key or picker only for the instant it is struck or flashed.

rules.name: The Shown Mechanism Rule
rules.body: Every converter surface pairs its result with a code table that shows, per key or cell, the source, the target and how often it was used.

rules.name: The Struck Key Rule
rules.body: Motion only ever answers the user: a keystroke, a conversion, a copy, a setting, a menu or a page change. The one exception is the single entrance when a page loads; nothing else moves on its own, nothing loops but the focused caret, and everything stops under reduced motion.

dos: **Do** take every colour from the eleven role variables so all five papers work unchanged in both modes.
**Do** define a light and a dark token set for any new paper, and check its accent against its own keycap before adding `--heat-ink`.
**Do** keep the accent for live state and the single primary action: used and struck keys, caret, focus, selection, the lead count, the chosen paper and layout, Copy.
**Do** set codes, counts, labels and typed text in Martian Mono (uppercase 11px at 0.06em for labels) and add the `--script` stack wherever user or mapped text can appear.
**Do** put the source legend top-left and the target bottom-right on every cap, and drive its tint from the heat ink by usage.
**Do** build structure with 1px rules: strong ink for frames, light rules inside, dashed for gaps and cuts.
**Do** keep new motion short, on the shared ease-out curve, tied to a user action, and switched off under reduced motion.
**Do** draw icons as inline SVG with a 1.75 round stroke in `currentColor`.
donts: **Don't** use gradients, textures, or drop shadows on resting surfaces; the settings panel and an open listbox are the only shadows.
**Don't** use red; the warning ink is burnt sienna in light mode (amber, or peach on Blueprint, in dark) and appears only on a non-zero miss count.
**Don't** add a second accent or a second primary button to a page.
**Don't** shrink the keyboard below legibility on a phone; split it into half-boards instead.
**Don't** use icon fonts, emoji or text glyphs as interface icons.
**Don't** couple paper and mode back into one theme list; they are two independent choices.
